newsitem.title: UK: Report criticises former British minister.
newsitem.headline: Report criticises former British minister.

text.p: The British Parliament's ethics commissioner said on Thursday there was "compelling" evidence that former trade minister Neil Hamilton accepted cash from businessman Mohammed al-Fayed in return for lobbying parliament on his behalf.

"The way in which these payments were received and concealed fell well below the standards expected of members of parliament," Sir Gordon Downey said in a long-awaited report into sleaze allegations against Hamilton and other Conservatives.

The report, presented to parliament's Standards and Privileges Committee, said another former minister, Tim Smith, received between 18,000 pounds ($30,150) and 25,000 pounds from Fayed in a manner which also fell below standards expected of legislators.

It made less serious criticisms of two other former Conservative members of parliament -- Sir Andrew Bowden for failing to declare an election donation from parliamentary lobbyist Ian Greer and Sir Michael Grylls for deliberately misleading a parliamentary committee about payments by Greer.

Downey said Hamilton, who dramatically lost his seat to an independent anti-corruption candidate at the May 1 election, received hospitality from Fayed at his luxury Ritz Hotel in Paris without registering this as he should have.
He said Hamilton also "deliberately misled" then Trade and Industry Secretary Michael Heseltine about a financial relationship with Greer.
